platform.windows: compiles; the Windows session path is T6 and no Windows QUIC run has been recorded
platform.note: All QUIC runs are loopback on macOS arm64. A platform difference must be reproduced against the same-platform Mihomo; nothing is claimed for a platform that was not run.

transitive: rand 0.10.4 / rand_pcg 0.10.2 (quinn-proto only; the workspace keeps rand 0.8)
quicDependencyProfile.offlineSource: ~/.cargo/registry/cache (the pinned index is available); no network access was used
notCached: h3 / h3-quinn / qpack crates: Hysteria2 uses the in-tree minimal HTTP/3 client instead
JLS-TLS / jls-quic-go equivalents: shadowquic cannot be expressed with rustls/quinn
boringtun / wireguard / smoltcp / etherparse: no WireGuard transport or IP stack
tailscale / zerotier / easytier / openvpn crates: no mesh or OpenVPN stack
quicDependencyProfile.memory: Per dial: one UDP Endpoint and one QUIC Connection. Transport windows are capped for T7: stream receive 512 KiB, connection receive 2 MiB, send 2 MiB, datagram buffers 64 KiB, crypto buffer 16 KiB (quinn defaults are 1.25 MB / VarInt::MAX / 10 MB / ~1 MB). No pool is implemented. T7 must measure the whole iOS extension against 40,000,000 bytes; this file records the dependency and the chosen caps, not a device measurement.

tuic.implemented: TUIC v5 over QUIC: TLS 1.3 (ALPN h3), uuid/password authentication via the TLS exporter token, one bidirectional Connect stream per TCP target; ip/sni/skip-cert-verify/disable-sni/heartbeat-interval/request-timeout
rejected: token (v4 / BLAKE3 TKN; no blake3 crate offline)
tuic.peer: pinned Mihomo listeners: type: tuic (users map) + a controlled quinn peer in tests/quic_peers.rs

hysteria.implemented: Hysteria v1 over QUIC (ALPN hysteria): binary ClientHello/ServerHello on a control stream (auth/auth-str, up/down), one request stream per TCP target
hysteria.peer: controlled quinn server implementing transport/hysteria/core/protocol.go (no Mihomo listener exists)

hysteria2.implemented: Hysteria2 over QUIC (ALPN h3): HTTP/3 POST /auth with Hysteria-Auth/Hysteria-CC-RX/Hysteria-Padding, status 233, then a 0x401 TCP request frame per session; up/down, handshake-timeout
rejected: obfs (Salamander/Gecko packet obfuscation needs a custom UDP socket wrapper)
initial/max stream and connection receive windows
hysteria2.peer: pinned Mihomo listeners: type: hysteria2 (users map)

shadowquic.reason: the pinned client uses JLS, a custom TLS extension, and a modified QUIC stack (jls-tls + jls-quic-go); rustls/quinn cannot express it and no JLS crate is in the offline cache
shadowquic.owner: T10 rejected; a JLS-capable TLS/QUIC stack would be a separate task

wireguard.reason: the pinned outbound terminates WireGuard (Noise IK, cookie, transport keys) and exposes TCP/UDP through a gVisor netstack; this kernel has no WireGuard transport or IP stack, and no boringtun/wireguard crate is offline
wireguard.owner: device/TUN ownership is T6/T7; the transport would be a separate task

tailscale.reason: the pinned outbound (with_gvisor) embeds the tailscale.com control plane and a gVisor netstack; no Rust tailscale stack is offline

zerotier.reason: the pinned outbound wraps zerotier-go (identity, planet, control protocol, crypto) plus a gVisor netstack; no Rust zerotier stack is offline

easytier.reason: the pinned outbound embeds the easytier-go host/instance (peer discovery, encryption, KCP/QUIC proxies) plus a netstack; no Rust easytier stack is offline

openvpn.reason: the pinned outbound implements OpenVPN (TLS control channel, data ciphers, tls-auth/tls-crypt) and exposes TCP/UDP through a gVisor netstack; no Rust OpenVPN stack is offline

deviceLayerOwnership.note: T10 delivers only protocol adaptation and the verifiable transport. Device/TUN selection, descriptor ownership, routing and switching stay with T6 (desktop/Android) and T7 (iOS packetFlow). No family in this task installs a TUN device or claims device ownership.
